unmapped_findings: Charpy U-notch impact absorbing energy (KU2) of the 1.3Al steel in the as-quenched (WQ) condition was 23 ± 2 J (Table 2 and Fig. 1(b)); there is no dedicated impact-toughness slot in the property schema, so it is recorded here. Source: b0035, b0039, figure_001, figure_002.

The 1.3Al steel fractured prior to reaching its maximum tensile strength during the room-temperature tensile test in the as-quenched (1.3Al,WQ) condition, with a total elongation of 4.3 ± 0.9 %. Source: b0034.

No fracture toughness (KIC/KQ) value was reported for the as-quenched (WQ) condition; the mechanical property table lists a dash for WQ while KIC is given only for the 2 h tempered conditions (0Al,2 h = 97.6 MPa·m^1/2; 1.3Al,2 h = 108.0 MPa·m^1/2). Source: b0039, figure_002.

The microstructural data quantified in the paper (retained austenite contents of 1.8 % for 1.3Al and 1.0 % for 0Al, dislocation densities of ~2.20 × 10^15 m^-2 for 1.3Al and ~2.01 × 10^15 m^-2 for 0Al, needle-like ε-carbides 100–500 nm long/2–4 nm thick, and coherent B2-NiAl clusters with number density 4.88 × 10^24 m^-3 and equivalent radius 0.57 nm) are reported for the tempered condition, not for the as-quenched (WQ) sample, and are therefore not attributed to this sample. Source: b0042, b0052, b0069.
